The shadowing path is blocked — the built-in send_email is used. So not_exploitable_as_configured: true. Still give a vector for residual path.

Residual path: attacker's MCP server could still offer other tools under namespaced, pinned names? Pinning drops anything not pinned. If pinned clean manifest, tools are constrained. Residual: none meaningful. Vector: AV:N (MCP server reachable via network; attacker controls server — remote). Actually preconditions: agent connected to attacker-controlled MCP server — AT:P? Fixed config requires pinning, so attacker's shadowed tool is dropped. Remaining: send_email goes through built-in stub, no exfiltration to attacker.

AIVSS: LC: attacker-controlled language via MCP manifest — but that's indirect? Manifest description reaches the model. It's ingested content influencing behavior → I. But with fix, shadowing prevented; manifest must match pin. If attacker controls the pinned server... assume fixed config makes tool descriptions pinned/reviewed → M (validated fields)? Pinning reduces to reviewed manifest — arguably M. I'll say LC: M? Hmm, evidence: descriptions scanned for injection patterns, args validated, names can't collide. Still attacker text (description) reaches model if pinned (i.e., it was reviewed). Fixed binding → LC M, CP N (session, no persistence on this path), AP C (relay across components within same agent? shadowing blocked → N), ES N (fixed allowlisted binding enforced), RH: no evaluator on path; reachable_proxy? No reward channel evidence → X? Set reachable_proxy null, isolation null → X.

CVSS residual vector: since not exploitable, give low vector. AV:N (remote MCP server), AC:L, AT:P (requires connected attacker-controlled MCP server — a condition attacker can't force), PR:L? The MCP server operator... PR:N? Attacker is the MCP server operator who doesn't own agent's assets. UI:A (user asks agent to email — passive? User must interact normally → P). Actually with fix, impact is none: VC:N VI:N VA:N, SC/SI/SA N.
